findings.title: Overwrite guard is in a function the CLI review path never calls
findings.description: T12 (task file 1, lines 233-236) adds archive-before-overwrite only to `save_review_file` (persistence.py:220). `save_review_result` (persistence.py:257-314) is what `sq review code` uses (cli/commands/review.py:746). It writes with `path.write_text` at line 303 and never calls `save_review_file`. Criterion 7 cannot pass as written, and the data-loss hazard stays open on the main path. Fix: put the guard in a shared write helper that both functions call, and test it through `save_review_result`.

findings.title: Archived copies overwrite each other
findings.description: T12 copies the prior file to `archive/{original filename}`. A second overwrite replaces the first archived copy, so criterion 7's "nothing is silently destroyed" fails on the second re-run. T13 tests only one overwrite. The slice design (Decision 7, lines 259-267) also specifies "original name," so the fix needs a design decision. Fix: give each archived copy a distinct name, chosen with the PM, and add a test with two consecutive overwrites.

findings.title: cf archive check is sequenced after the guard it gates
findings.description: The slice design (lines 381-383) requires the cf archive-scanning check to be "sequenced before Part D lands." In the breakdown, T14 follows T12 and T13, and T13's commit (line 272) lands Part D before the check runs. The note at lines 253-255 blocks only marking T12 done. Fix: move T14 ahead of T12. The PM question inside it can run alongside T1–T11.

findings.title: New `review/addressed/` package imports from the pipeline package
findings.description: T3 (file 1, lines 109-113) says `verification.py`'s `RoundDiff` import "stays... in the pipeline→review direction." After the move, `verification.py` lives under `review/`, so the import runs review→pipeline. `RoundDiff` is defined at `screens.py:34`. The same problem recurs in T5, where `judge_residue_core` takes `diff: RoundDiff` (judge.py:94, imported at judge.py:21), and in T21, where `review/resolution.py` imports `RoundDiff` and `screen_byte_identical` from pipeline. This recreates the review↔pipeline cycle the F002 fix (slice design lines 141-155) was meant to remove. Fix: move `RoundDiff` into `review/addressed/`, decide where the context-free byte-identical check lives, and correct the T3 wording before starting.

findings.title: Judge unreadable-response and timeout paths are untested
findings.description: Criterion 9 requires a judge transport failure and an unreadable judge response to yield UNKNOWN. T25 covers only the `failed=True` path, and T26 tests only a transport that raises. No task tests an unparseable response (`is_parse_failure`, parsing.py:80) or a timeout, which the data-flow section also lists. Fix: add both cases to T26.

findings.title: Injection cap is undefined
findings.description: T25 (file 2, lines 212-221) says to reuse "whatever threshold 305's architecture already defines" and to flag the PM if there is none. In the code, `findings_addressed/` has no cap and no `get_config` call. The only defined cap is `review.max_total_injection_bytes`, read at review_client.py:238 for review-prompt injection. Criterion 9 requires the warning to name the cap, so it should be a named config key read without a hard-coded default (CLAUDE.md). Fix: name the key in T25, and get the PM's decision on whether it applies to the judge diff before implementation.

findings.title: Empty `git log` output is not handled
findings.description: T19 covers a non-zero or `None` result from `git log -1 -- <review>`. An uncommitted review exits 0 with empty stdout, so the task would pass `""` as the diff base. T19 also contradicts itself: lines 107-109 say the caller must validate the ref with `run_git`, while lines 115-119 say the function returns what it resolved and the caller classifies it. Fix: treat empty output as an explicit UNKNOWN+WARNING case, and keep one of the two statements.

findings.title: Reviewed-SHA stamp is tested on one path only
findings.description: Criterion 1 requires `reviewedSha` from both the CLI and pipeline paths. T11 accepts "save_review_result (or the pipeline review action, whichever is more directly testable)," so only one path gets tested. T10 also calls `save_review_result` "the CLI path," but the pipeline action calls it at review.py:255 and calls `format_review_markdown` directly at line 265. Fix: test both paths, and have T10 name each call site it changes.

findings.title: Verify-failure branch of the overwrite guard is untested
findings.description: T12 (lines 238-246) requires reading the archive back and aborting on mismatch. T13 tests only an unwritable directory. Criterion 10 covers "failed or unverifiable" copies, so the read-back branch has no test. Fix: add a test that forces a read-back mismatch and asserts the abort, an unchanged original, and an ERROR log.

findings.title: "Review discovery" is tested for one function only
findings.description: Criterion 11 names `discover_judge_results` and "review discovery." T32 tests only `discover_judge_results` (metrology/discovery.py:27). `capture.py:97` has a separate `{index}-review.*` glob that the breakdown never names. A resolution filename cannot match it, but the criterion requires a test. Fix: name the second function in T32 and add its test.

findings.title: "Passes unchanged" contradicts the import edits T1 requires
findings.description: T1 edits imports in four `tests/pipeline/test_findings_addressed*.py` files. T6 says that if any test "needed rewriting, the extraction changed behavior — stop." Once T1 has run, T6 cannot pass as written. Decision 4 and criterion 12 say "unchanged." Fix: define "unchanged" as no changes to assertions or fixture logic, with import-path edits allowed, and state that in T1 and T6.

findings.title: Commit markers do not use the `**Commit**:` form
findings.description: Both files write `Commit:` without bold, six markers in file 1 and thirteen in file 2. CLAUDE.md commits only at `**Commit**:` markers and otherwise at the end of each top-level task. Read literally, the fallback applies, so T1 would be committed before T2 has verified the move. The T24 marker also uses `fix:` for new screen behavior, which the commit-type rules classify as `feat`. Fix: switch to `**Commit**:` and correct the T24 prefix.

findings.title: T36 cites a test file that does not exist and a name that is taken
findings.description: `tests/cli/commands/test_review.py` does not exist. The CLI review tests are `tests/cli/test_review_format.py`, `test_review_profile.py`, and `test_review_save.py`. `tests/cli/test_review_resolve.py` already exists and tests slice-number resolution (`_resolve_slice_number`), so a new `sq review resolve` test cannot use that name. Fix: cite the real test idiom and choose a distinct file name.

findings.title: Shared YAML helper is left open, and a duplicate is allowed
findings.description: T29 (file 2, lines 270-278) lets the implementer either promote `_yaml_safe` (evidence.py:96) to shared code or leave a copy and add "an equivalent" in the new module. The design requires one shared helper, and CLAUDE.md's DRY rule forbids the copy. T29 also bundles helper extraction with the full `render_resolution` renderer. Fix: choose the shared helper, and split extraction from rendering.

findings.title: Breakdown is heavier than a 3/5 slice warrants
findings.description: The slice is rated 3/5 overall, but the breakdown has 40 tasks, 18 of them test or verification. Part 0 is a move with no behavior change and takes eight tasks. T2, T4, and T6 each re-run the same subset, and T7 (exports) and T8 (full suite) can fold into T5 and T6. In file 2, several 1/5 tests immediately follow their own 1/5 implementation (T15/T16, T23/T24, T27/T28) and could be one task each. Fix: merge those pairs and the verification-only steps, keeping test-with pairing. The two-file split is reasonable at this size.

findings.title: "Empty diff" scope is ambiguous
findings.description: T21 says the diff is empty "against the CONCERN+ findings' scope." Criterion 3 says "an empty diff since reviewedSha." A scoped reading would change the outcome. Fix: state that emptiness is measured over the whole base..HEAD plus working-tree diff.

findings.title: Load-test rule may apply to the judge leg
findings.description: The judge leg makes a network call through `run_review_with_profile`. The slice restates no NFR, so the reviewer's load-test clause does not trigger. The project's Python rules require a load test for network paths. Confirm with the PM whether a single-shot CLI judge call falls under that rule. If it does, add a `tests/load/` task and a CI gate.

findings.title: Stale cross-reference in T33
findings.description: T33 says it sequences "T17→T33," which includes itself. The range should be T17→T32.
